title: Unbanning is decided by a binding Governance Poll, not by the moderator who imposed the ban
content:
A.2.7.1.2.1.1.3 makes bans "by default permanent," then supplies the only route back: "Ranked Delegates can propose the unbanning of users by publishing a forum post that states the handle(s)... and the rationale." The post must tag the Core Facilitator, "who will in turn prepare a binary Governance Poll through the Operational Weekly Cycle to be published on the Voting Portal as soon as reasonably possible. The outcome of the Governance Poll is binding."

The structural point is that the power to reverse a ban sits with a different body than the power to impose one. A moderator can exclude; only the electorate can readmit. That asymmetry means a ban is never quietly negotiated away, and equally that no moderator can permanently exclude someone the community wants present.

The Ranked Delegate gate is the filter that keeps this workable. Requiring a delegate to attach their name and a rationale means every banned user cannot force a poll on their own — someone with governance standing must first judge the case worth the electorate's time. The Core Facilitator's role is reduced to mechanically preparing the poll, so it cannot be blocked by the same office that may have imposed the ban.

The closing provision extends the remedy's reach: "Where identity can be proven, the ban on unbanned users will be lifted across all communication channels." A reinstatement is ecosystem-wide rather than per-venue, which matches the ecosystem-wide effect of exclusion — but it conditions on provable identity, which is exactly the thing the next section admits is unreliable.
description: Bans are permanent by default, but any Ranked Delegate can force a binary poll by posting a rationale and tagging the Core Facilitator, and the poll's outcome binds.
